blocks.text: This book counts progress in pages, not chapters. Use the + and − buttons at the top to move your page count by hand.
Marking a chapter as done here doesn’t change the page count: a chapter can be twenty pages or two.
Slow reading isn’t about reading less. It means giving each page the time it needs, and no more.
A good reading place has few interruptions and a surface for notes. Comfort matters less than continuity.
Tip: the same place every day makes starting easier.
Notes in the margin are a conversation with the text. Write questions, objections and links to other chapters.
A margin note is a question you’ll be glad to find later.
Stop at the end of an idea, not at the end of a page. It’s easier to pick up a thought than half a sentence.
Finish the paragraph you are in.
Write one line saying where you are.
